Turn spoken English or Russian into clearer engineering text with selectable processing levels.

- **None** keeps the original transcript in the spoken language and skips the editing model's download, startup and requests.
- **Light** cleans up grammar, word order, fillers, repetition and spoken corrections while keeping the sequence of ideas. Existing settings remain on Light.
- **Heavy** organizes rambling speech into coherent engineering paragraphs or task lists, preserving distinct details, constraints, uncertainty and questions.
- Adds a built-in dictionary of **164 engineering terms**, including English and Russian pronunciation variants for names such as `three.js`, Node.js and TypeScript. Only relevant hints are supplied; personal glossary spellings take precedence.
- Strengthens rules for numeric digits, percentages and technical spellings. Backticked code and existing emojis remain protected.
- If a source question loses every question mark outside code, the app retries once with a preservation reminder. A second failure is held for review instead of inserted.
- Debug reports now include the selected processing level and whether the engineering dictionary is enabled.

Open **Settings → Editing → Text processing** to choose a level. For Heavy, **Qwen 4B** performed better than 2B in the focused quality checks. Small models can still miss formatting rules or alter meaning. Custom instructions continue to override the built-in processing rules; use **Restore default instructions** to adopt the presets. TranslateGemma retains its translation-only behavior.

Stable release for **Windows x64**, **Apple silicon** and **Intel Macs**. Windows reuses the existing shared engine cache and uses a standard ZIP without a `.` folder. Mac builds remain ad-hoc signed until Developer ID signing and notarization are configured; see the installation instructions in the README if macOS requests approval.
